checks.claim: C1 (incl. new general-k approximate-identity paragraph): homogeneity, scaling, the exact adjacent one-chain diagram and its delta convention
checks.reason: Homogeneity and lambda-scaling are unchanged and correct. Dirichlet check: the integral over sum h < t of the product of h_odd^1 h_even^{-a0}, times 2^{-k}, equals [Gamma(1-a0)/2]^k t^{(3-a0)k}/Gamma(1+(3-a0)k). At k=1 this is c0/2; at k=2, a0=0 it is 1/2880. The new paragraph is substantively correct. Write u_j = y_2j - y_2j-1, and let Psi(u) be the integral over the k free odd coordinates. At u=0 the even indicators |u_j| < h_2j equal one near zero because h_2j > 0. The odd indicators converge pointwise off the hyperplanes |y_2j-1 - y_2j-3| = h_2j-1 (and |y_1| = h_1), a Lebesgue-null set. Bounded convergence on a bounded region then gives continuity of Psi at 0, and convolution with mass-one Gaussians yields Psi(0). Uniform bound: the Green indicators force all positions into [-t,t] at every smoothing level. Each smoothed pair integrates to at most 2t on [-t,t]^2, giving (2t)^k * 2^{-2k} = t^k/2^k. Domination: the times-cube integral of the product of k disjoint-pair factors |s-r|^{-a0} equals (2t^{2-a0}/((1-a0)(2-a0)))^k < infinity, and the increment-to-time map is unimodular. Dominated convergence is valid for each fixed k. The wording 'free paired positions converge to the diagonal restriction' is informal (see minor findings).

checks.reason: E|U-V| = s/2 + r^2/(6s) <= 2s/3 for r <= s. Convexity gives the kernel bound >= (3/2)^alpha s^{1-alpha} r. Then 2 * int_0^1 ds int_0^s (s-r)^{-a0} s^{1-alpha} r dr = 2/[(1-a0)(2-a0)(4-alpha-a0)]. At 1/2,1/2 the bound is (8/9) sqrt(3/2), about 1.089, which exceeds 2/3 = 2a_1; G1's E X_2 formula gives a_1 = 1/(0.5*1*2*3) = 1/3. White static check: 8a_2 + 4a_1^2 = 11/2160 + 60/2160 = 71/2160 and A_2 = 44/2160, a difference of 1/80. The small-time remainder argument O(t^{2beta}) holds for convergent nonnegative series. checks.claim: C4: a0 -> 1 Riesz obstruction and all parameter/prefactor quantifiers
checks.reason: H_alpha(0) = 2^{3-alpha}/(2(3-alpha)) = 2^{2-alpha}/(3-alpha). The approximate identity eps * int_0^1 v^{-1+eps} H(v) dv -> H(0) gives (1-a0) b_1 -> c_alpha 2^{2-alpha}/[(1-alpha)(2-alpha)(3-alpha)]. From E X_2, a_1 -> c_alpha/[(1-alpha)^2(2-alpha)(3-alpha)]. Hence (1-a0) A_1/a_1 -> 2^{2-alpha}(1-alpha) > 0. So C = 2^{4-alpha}, which is independent of a0, fails for a0 near 1 at fixed 0 < alpha < 1. The result is correctly restricted to Riesz, asserts no numerical threshold, and does not refute an (alpha,a0)-dependent C. The static-endpoint quantifier defect that caused the v1 C4 FAIL is resolved (R1-R3).

checks.claim: C5 (incl. new explicit coefficient optimization): conditional sufficiency of (MC)/(DT) via the imported first-moment theorem; both remain open
checks.reason: (MC) with A_0 = a_0 = 1 gives E u^2(t) <= E u(C^{1/beta} t), so limsup t^{-kappa} log E u^2 <= C^{1/(3-alpha)} L*. New optimization: Theorem 1.2 gives, for any L > L* (see minor findings), a T with E u(t) <= exp(L t^kappa) for t >= T. Nonnegativity gives a_n t^{beta n} <= E u(t). With t = (qn/L)^{1/kappa}, L t^kappa = qn, and t^{beta n} = (qn/L)^{qn} because beta/kappa = 3-alpha = q. Hence a_n <= e^{qn}(L/(qn))^{qn} = [(eL/q)^q]^n n^{-qn} <= B^n/(n!)^q, using n! <= n^n. This holds for n large enough that t >= T, and the finitely many earlier finite coefficients are absorbed into B. No Section-8 import is needed. (DT) then gives ||X_n||_2 <= (CB)^{n/2} t^{beta n/2}/(n!)^{q/2}. The l^r-vs-l^1 inequality with r = q/2 >= 1 gives exp(r z^{1/r}) with z^{1/r} proportional to t^kappa. Minkowski is legitimate because u = sum X_n in L^2 (G0). Both comparisons are explicitly unproved.
